subject: Request: Dedicated capacity pricing exception & commit structure — Olive Health
messages:
From: Katie Morgan <katie@olivehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@procuro.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing and commit ask

Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Olive Health is evaluating dedicated GPU pools for our inference tier. Two quick asks as we prepare procurement: 

1) Pricing: we have a competitive proposal that includes a 35% discount on list for an annual commit. Can Redwood match or come close?
2) Pool sizing / throughput guarantees: our engineering team estimates a steady-state of ~120 rps (avg token length ~300) with 95th percentile latency target of 200ms. What pool size and SLO can you guarantee at that throughput?
3) Commit structure: we prefer a 12-month reserved commit but need a clear burst/buffer policy for predictable spikes during monthly retros.

Attached is our SOW draft and a small throughput profile export. Please advise pricing flexibility and any prerequisites for the SLA.

Best,
Katie
VP Product
Olive Health

Attachments: OLIVE-SOW-draft.docx (docx), throughput_profile.csv (csv)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morgan <katie@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@procuro.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing and commit ask

Katie —

Appreciate the clear asks and the SOW. Quick responses up front:
- We can put together a tailored term sheet for a 12-month reserved commit.
- We typically recommend a GPU pool equivalent to ~12 A100-class cards for the profile you described (this maps to continuous throughput ~110–140 rps depending on batching and KV cache hit). Monica will follow with a sizing note.
- Regarding discounting: we have standard tiered commit discounts; for strategic deals we can consider an exception (credits or % off) but that requires manager approval and a short exec sign-off.

I'll attach an initial term sheet (v3) with two concession options: 1) a 25% committed discount plus 2 weeks free burst credits, or 2) a 30% discount with a minimum 18-month revenue commitment. Please review and tell us which path you'd prefer; we can accelerate approvals if Olive confirms ARR/commit expectations.

Next steps: Monica will confirm the sizing recommendation, and I'll pull finance/legal for the exception paperwork.

Thanks —
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Katie Morgan <katie@olivehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing and commit ask

Katie / Sergio —

Quick technical note on sizing and SLOs: based on the supplied throughput_profile.csv and the brief (300 token average):
- Baseline recommendation: 12 x GPU equivalent (A100 v3 equivalence) configured with 8-worker serving per GPU. Expected sustained throughput ~120 rps with 95th percentile generation latency ~180–230ms depending on tokenization variance.
- Autoscale buffer: we recommend 2x burst capacity (on-demand warm pool) for predictable spikes; this can be gated by a policy that costs burst usage separately as credits.
- KV/prefix caching: enabling our prefix cache will raise effective throughput by ~15% for repeated prompt shapes (common for your UI flows).

If you want, we can run a short proof-of-load (3–4 days) on a trial pool to validate these numbers. That typically helps procurement agree on a narrower SLA window.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Katie Morgan <katie@olivehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting discount exception for Olive Health (strategic) — RDW-7281

Rishi / Lauren —

Summary: Olive Health is a strategic prospect in the digital health vertical with strong product-market fit and potential expansion across three hospitals if the pilot goes well. They asked for a competitive match to a 35% off list proposal. Our standard committed discount schedule would put them at ~20–22% for the commit level they're proposing.

Proposed concession options I recommend presenting (choose one):
A) Revenue-first: 30% off list on a 12-month commit (RDW revenue recognition across 12 months). No change to SLA; 1 month of burst credits included.
B) Lower upfront discount: 25% off list + guaranteed 2-week dedicated PoC (trial pool billed at 25% of committed rate during PoC) and ability to convert credits to first-month usage.

Justification:
- Market defense: competitor is already in PoC with one of Olive's pilots.
- Upside: potential to expand from pilot to 3 enterprise sites within 12–18 months.
- Minimal incremental risk: we keep commit + revenue recognition intact and limit credits.

Please advise whether you approve either option or prefer escalation to Naomi for exec sign-off. If approved, legal will issue a concession addendum and finance will set up a credits ledger tied to deal RDW-7281.

Thanks,
Sergio

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting discount exception for Olive Health (strategic) — RDW-7281

Sergio —

I reviewed the background and the proposed options. I can provisionally approve Option A (30% off list, 1 month burst credits) contingent on:
1) Naomi's final approval as revenue-owner for strategic exceptions;
2) Sales to secure a signed LOI indicating the 12-month commit and expected monthly consumption band;
3) Legal to insert a clause restricting credits to non-transferrable usage, and Finance to confirm anticipated margin impact.

Please escalate to Naomi with the LOI and the final recommended option. If Naomi signs off we will route for a one-off pricing exception code and addendum.

Lauren
Head of Sales Operations

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Katie Morgan <katie@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Approved concession for Olive Health (RDW-7281)

Team / Katie —

After reviewing the context and the LOI received from Olive, I approve a limited exception: Option A with modifications. Final terms below — these are binding only after DocuSign: 

- 12-month committed contract.
- 30% off list across committed spend for Year 1 only. Year 2 reverts to standard committed discount schedule unless otherwise negotiated.
- One month of burst credits equivalent to the committed daily rate; credits expire after 90 days and are only usable against inference usage for Olive Health account.
- SLA: Redwood will target the 95th percentile latency ≤ 220ms for the agreed throughput band. Remedies are operational (priority support and capacity uplift) not financial credits.
- Legal addendum: credits non-transferrable; standard data/access clauses to remain.

Next steps: Legal to draft concession addendum and attach to the term sheet. Finance to create concession code RDW-CRED-7281. Sergio/Rishi to send DocuSign link to Katie and secure signature. Monica to schedule 3-day proof-of-load in week of Jun 22 if Olive wants to validate.

Good work — this is the right balance of competitiveness and protection for Redwood.

Naomi Feldman
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v3_final.pdf
